# About you

## Stance
Use only the athlete's volunteered information and Tempo-derived training context. Coach training decisions; do not diagnose medical conditions or prescribe treatment. If something sounds medical or outside coaching, urge the athlete to seek a qualified professional and keep training conservative.

## Goal
You are training for the Lakeshore Marathon on Sun Nov 15, aiming for 3:30. This will be your fourth marathon, and your personal best is 3:41 from two years ago.

## Schedule
You run five days a week: Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat and Sun. Mon and Fri are fixed rest days because of work travel.

Weekday runs are early, around 6am before work, capped near an hour. Saturday is an easy hour and Sunday is the long run.

Typical volume is 6 to 7 hours a week, with more on long-run weeks.

## Running history
You have run three marathons already, best 3:41. You eased off in June and have built back to about 30 miles a week through July.

Recent weeks show four easy runs of roughly 5 to 6 miles and a long run of about 10.8 miles on Sun Aug 2.

## Injuries and constraints
You are healthy right now. You had shin splints in your first marathon block, so you prefer to ramp mileage up carefully.

Work travel takes you away about one week in six. Mon and Fri rest days cannot move.

## Preferences
You train mostly on flat paved loops and a canal path, with one hillier route on Thursdays. You want easy days to be properly easy and you are happy to work hard on quality days.

You like to know why a session is in the plan. Shoes: Brooks Ghost 16 for daily miles, Saucony Endorphin Speed 4 for workouts.

## Current status
You are at about 30 miles a week with a long run near 11 miles. Units are miles. Heart rate zones are set custom, with easy running in 112 – 150 bpm.

recentHistory.analysis:
## Why this shape

Last week was a planned step back and you came out of it feeling bouncy, so this week rebuilds to around 42 miles with the long run going to 16 and one quality session touching marathon pace. You are 11 weeks out from Lakeshore, which is the right window to start layering goal-pace work into the long run instead of only doing it on Thursday.

## The quality day

Thursday is marathon-pace reps: 2 x 3 miles at 8:00/mi with 3 minutes easy jog between. Two three-mile blocks are long enough to feel like race rhythm but short enough that you are not hanging on in the second half, which is where pacing errors show up. If 8:00 feels forced in the first rep, settle at 8:05 and we will tighten it over the next few weeks.

## The long run

Sixteen miles Sunday, mostly steady, with the last 3 miles lifted to marathon-pace effort. This is the first time this block we are putting goal pace on tired legs, and it is the single most useful workout between here and taper. Start the first 10 miles honest and easy (9:40 – 9:55), then roll into 8:00 – 8:05 for the finish.

## Easy running and context

Easy pace has crept from 9:50 to 9:34 at the same 144 HR, which is exactly the aerobic drift you want. Keep Tue, Wed and Sat properly easy — if HR climbs toward 150 early, slow down. Fueling for the long runs matters more now that we are over two hours, and I have put specifics in the answer.

recentHistory.analysis:
## Why a cutback now

You jumped 7 miles week over week on 6.4 hours of sleep and high work stress, and Saturday's easy run already felt like work. That is the moment to pull back a notch, not push through. The pattern we want in a build is three up, one down, and you have had three up weeks in a row.

## What stays, what shrinks

Long run holds near 12 miles so you keep the aerobic stimulus but with less total load around it. Thursday's workout drops to three marathon-pace miles with full recoveries — enough to touch 8:00/mi cleanly without the Z4 time you got from the longer tempo. Easy days stay the same length but I want them genuinely easy, HR under 150, pace closer to 9:50 than 9:30.

## Looking ahead

If this week lands well, next week goes back up toward 40 with a 16-mile long run and a longer quality session. If sleep stays short or anything in the shins whispers, we hold flat another week — the race is still 11 weeks out and the base is there.

## Why this shape

Last week jumped about 10% in miles and the overall effort score climbed well above your 3-week average, so this week holds mileage flat and keeps the quality session shorter. You are healthy and the long run went well, but a second big jump on top of 25°C mornings is where shin trouble tends to creep back in.

## The quality day

Thursday moves from a straight tempo to marathon-pace miles with full recoveries. Goal pace for 3:30 is 8:00/mi, and short reps let you touch that pace in the heat without the heart rate drift you would get from a long block. If 8:00 feels forced, run 8:05 – 8:10 and we will build from there.

## Easy running

Keep Tuesday, Wednesday and Saturday properly easy, which for you right now means roughly 9:45 – 10:00/mi and heart rate under 150. Your Wednesday run drifted into Z3 last week; start the first mile slower and let it settle.

## Long run

Thirteen miles on Sunday, steady, no marathon-pace finish this week. Start before sunrise if you can, carry fluid, and if the heat index is brutal, cut it to 11 rather than grind.
